name: Nepal
note: Each claim is one rendered observation on the canonical page. claims.title: Rise of the Licchavi dynasty
claims.summary: The Licchavis establish the first well-documented dynasty of the Kathmandu Valley, using Sanskrit, minting coins and linking India and Tibet by trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-450-rise-of-the-licchavi-dynasty, claim TL:NPL:event:450:rise-of-the-licchavi-dynasty, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Licchavi stone inscriptions
claims.summary: Dense Licchavi-era inscriptions and chronicles make the valley one of the best-documented early states of the Himalayas, recording Hindu and Buddhist patronage alike.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-500-licchavi-stone-inscriptions, claim TL:NPL:event:500:licchavi-stone-inscriptions, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Traditional founding of Kathmandu
claims.summary: Tradition credits Raja Gunakamadeva with founding the town of Kathmandu during the Licchavi period; it would later give its name to the valley and the nation's capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-723-traditional-founding-of-kathmandu, claim TL:NPL:event:723:traditional-founding-of-kathmandu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Birth of the Buddha at Lumbini
claims.summary: Siddhartha Gautama, of the Shakya clan, is born at Lumbini to Queen Mayadevi and King Suddhodana of Kapilavastu; he later founds Buddhism.

sources.label: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-563bce-birth-of-the-buddha-at-lumbini, claim TL:NPL:event:563bce:birth-of-the-buddha-at-lumbini, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ashoka's pillar at Lumbini
claims.summary: The Mauryan emperor Ashoka visits Lumbini and erects an inscribed sandstone pillar, the earliest material evidence identifying the Buddha's birthplace.

sources.label: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-249bce-ashoka-s-pillar-at-lumbini, claim TL:NPL:event:249bce:ashoka-s-pillar-at-lumbini, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lumbini inscribed as World Heritage
claims.summary: UNESCO inscribes Lumbini on the World Heritage List, recognising it as the birthplace of the Buddha and a centre of Buddhist pilgrimage since the 3rd century BCE.

sources.label: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1997-lumbini-inscribed-as-world-heritage, claim TL:NPL:event:1997:lumbini-inscribed-as-world-heritage, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malla dynasty rules the valley
claims.summary: The Mallas govern the Kathmandu Valley, codifying Hindu-influenced law and patronising the Newar temple architecture for which the valley becomes famous.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1200-malla-dynasty-rules-the-valley, claim TL:NPL:event:1200:malla-dynasty-rules-the-valley, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Valley divided into three kingdoms
claims.summary: Yaksha Malla partitions the valley among his sons, founding the rival city-states of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur, which compete over Tibet–India trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1482-valley-divided-into-three-kingdoms, claim TL:NPL:event:1482:valley-divided-into-three-kingdoms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Durbar squares and Newar art
claims.summary: Malla patronage produces the palace squares, pagoda temples and stupas later recognised as the seven monument zones of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1300-the-durbar-squares-and-newar-art, claim TL:NPL:event:1300:the-durbar-squares-and-newar-art, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Conquest of the Kathmandu Valley
claims.summary: Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha captures Kathmandu in 1768 and the Malla kingdoms by 1769, unifying the hill states into the kingdom of Nepal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1768-conquest-of-the-kathmandu-valley, claim TL:NPL:event:1768:conquest-of-the-kathmandu-valley, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Anglo-Nepalese War
claims.summary: A border dispute with British India erupts into the Gurkha War; Nepali resistance is fierce but the East India Company prevails.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1814-anglo-nepalese-war, claim TL:NPL:event:1814:anglo-nepalese-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Sugauli
claims.summary: Nepal cedes the Tarai and western conquests and admits a British resident, but keeps its independence and monarchy — never becoming a colony.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1816-treaty-of-sugauli, claim TL:NPL:event:1816:treaty-of-sugauli, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jung Bahadur founds Rana rule
claims.summary: After a violent seizure of power, Jung Bahadur becomes prime minister for life with the hereditary title of Rana, sidelining the Shah kings for a century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1846-jung-bahadur-founds-rana-rule, claim TL:NPL:event:1846:jung-bahadur-founds-rana-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Revolution restores the monarchy
claims.summary: A palace revolt and popular movement end Rana dominance and restore the sovereignty of the Shah crown under King Tribhuvan.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1951-revolution-restores-the-monarchy, claim TL:NPL:event:1951:revolution-restores-the-monarchy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Panchayat autocracy
claims.summary: King Mahendra dissolves parliament in 1960 and bans parties; the 1962 constitution installs the partyless panchayat system under royal control.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1962-panchayat-autocracy, claim TL:NPL:event:1962:panchayat-autocracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: People's Movement restores democracy
claims.summary: Nationwide protests force King Birendra to legalise political parties and accept a multiparty parliamentary system, ending the panchayat era.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1990-people-s-movement-restores-democracy, claim TL:NPL:event:1990:people-s-movement-restores-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maoist insurgency
claims.summary: The Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist) wages a decade-long armed insurgency that kills more than 12,000 people before a 2006 UN-mediated peace accord.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-1996-maoist-insurgency, claim TL:NPL:event:1996:maoist-insurgency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Monarchy abolished, republic declared
claims.summary: A newly elected constituent assembly ends more than two centuries of Shah rule and declares Nepal a federal democratic republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-2008-monarchy-abolished-republic-declared, claim TL:NPL:event:2008:monarchy-abolished-republic-declared, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gorkha earthquake
claims.summary: A magnitude-7.8 quake near Gorkha kills about 9,000 people and devastates Kathmandu Valley heritage, including Durbar squares and the Dharahara tower.

sources.label: One Year After the M7.8 Nepal (Gorkha) Earthquake

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-2015-gorkha-earthquake, claim TL:NPL:event:2015:gorkha-earthquake, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Federal constitution promulgated
claims.summary: Nepal adopts a permanent constitution establishing a secular federal republic of seven provinces with a bicameral Federal Parliament.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Nepal: From the Buddha's birthplace and the valley of art to a Himalayan federal republic.", terralore.co/country/NPL/chronicle#ev-2015-federal-constitution-promulgated, claim TL:NPL:event:2015:federal-constitution-promulgated, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
